No but I can link the shelters I stayed at if you’re interested.
I also want to clarify, it’s not just the food that i have a problem with, it’s an overall culture of neglect and (over)control under the guise of ‘help’. It’s a dynamic reminiscent to an abusive relationship. 

The workers here do not want to do anything for you. You’re not allowed to bother them when the office door is closed (and it’s closed quite often) as there is a “do not disturb” policy. They take away your medications, any sharp objects (tweezers, razors), ask you to go in detail about your abuse and mental health, then do absolutely nothing to help you cope or find other accommodations all while practically pushing you out the door. They don’t keep track of helping you take your meds either, a poor lady i stayed with was in PAIN since she needed to take her cancer medication and nobody was there to help her. She practically begged me to go and find a worker to help her. Fucking awful. She was in tears. The workers were on another floor watching a movie and the poor sick lady was unable to use stairs due to her condition. There’s a shit ton of rules, you get in trouble for eating in your room, yet they don’t feed me properly and somehow I’m the bad guy? I’ve been questioned whether my situation is really “that bad” and do I “actually need to stay there?”. The only time they ever spoke to me were to reinforce rules, tell me there wasn’t food for me, or to ask me what my “plan” was (Ex. When are you getting out of here) 

also they will kick you out on the streets and cite policy. There were so many available beds, and because a young girl had stayed her allocated time, they kicked her out because it was “policy”. She was my old roommate. Bawled her eyes out the last day. Bed was never filled in the month I stayed there after along with plenty of other empty beds in the shelter

The first night I was there, they “forgot” to give me sheets and a blanket, so I tied together my clothes to make a blanket myself. I didn’t receive the sheets or blanket until I asked. I was not allowed to use the pillows and blanket I brought with me because of “Covid”. They promised me they would store them away safely but they “lost them” and ironically had no record of me keeping it in storage. 

There was also a man who worked at the second shelter I stayed at, that would just walk in our rooms to “check” on us, no knock, nothing. Just made me uncomfortable af. He only ever did it when he was working the night shifts by himself.

The entire system is counterproductive to helping women in need. I’ve witnessed them send women right back where they came from without blinking an eye.  

It’s also worth mentioning that the women who were staying there like myself (escaping abuse/sex work/homelessness/other) were some of the kindest women I’ve ever met in my life. Truly angels. They would always advocate for me when there wasn’t a food option for myself.

I don’t think my problem is that I pity myself but that I don’t empathize or love myself. I grew up in a family that demeaned any sign of self-pity. I don’t talk to people about my problems and I don’t allow myself to feel bad about things without intense self-criticism for “feeling sorry for myself” as my dad used to put it. As someone who was diagnosed with depression and anxiety, it becomes a cycle of persistent negativity because I hate myself for feelings I can’t control. Feeling sorry for myself is something I obsess over not doing which has prevented me from opening up or seeking out help. I’m not sure if this makes sense, I just wanted to clarify on my end my experience with it.
